title: WCAG 1.4.11 3:1 contrast for UI components
statement:
WCAG 1.4.11 requires the visual information needed to identify user interface components and their states (input borders, checkbox states, focus indicators) and the meaningful parts of graphics to reach 3:1 against adjacent colors, so pale-gray field borders on white and low-contrast icons fail.

Options:
- Visible field borders: Input borders at 3:1 or more against the page background, for example a #767676 border on #FFFFFF (about 4.54:1) (fits: clear, professional, trustworthy)
- Button fill or outline contrast: Solid button fills that reach 3:1 against their surroundings, or an outline that does (button text still needs 4.5:1) (fits: bold, confident, modern)
- Strong focus ring: Focus ring of 2px or thicker with at least 3:1 contrast against adjacent colors, for example #005FCC on white (about 6:1) (fits: accessible, technical, polished)
- Meaningful icons at 3:1: Icons that carry meaning without a text label at 3:1 or more; purely decorative icons are exempt (fits: minimal, clear, friendly)
- Chart legibility: Chart parts distinguished by direct labels, markers or patterns as well as color, with the required graphic parts at 3:1 (fits: data-driven, technical, analytical)
appliesWhen: Applies to: general web. Audience: general.

source.title: Understanding SC 1.4.11: Non-text Contrast, Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2
source.venue: W3C WCAG 2.2 (SC 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast, Level AA, introduced in WCAG 2.1 in 2018)
